summary: Defines GMPLS signaling extensions for Wavelength Switched Optical Networks. They cover cases such as configuring regeneration at certain nodes or setting the attributes of optical signals that equipment accepts or outputs.

eli5.summary: This gives a way to tell optical equipment exactly how to handle a beam of light along its route.

questions: how does gmpls signal optical wavelengths
what is the wson processing hop attribute tlv
what wavelength assignment methods does gmpls support
subtitle: How GMPLS signaling tells optical nodes which processing to apply and which wavelength-picking method to use along a path.

tldr.problem: In a wavelength switched optical network, nodes along a path may need to regenerate a signal or accept and output signals with specific attributes, and existing GMPLS signaling cannot express this. Networks that pick wavelengths hop by hop also have no way to say which method to use.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a WSON Processing Hop Attribute TLV, carried in the Hop Attributes subobjects of the ERO and RRO. It holds a ResourceBlockInfo sub-TLV for processing resources and a WavelengthSelection sub-TLV for wavelength assignment direction and method.
tldr.outcome: A node can be told what to do at a given hop and can report back what it used. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

today: RFC 7689 is a Proposed Standard and the data shows no obsoleting or updating RFC, so it remains the definition of these WSON signaling extensions.

sections.title: Introduction and Scope
sections.content:
RFC 7689 extends Generalized Multiprotocol Label Switching (GMPLS) signaling for Wavelength Switched Optical Networks (WSONs). A WSON is a WDM-based optical network in which switching is performed selectively based on the frequency of an optical signal.

The fundamental extensions allow simultaneous bidirectional wavelength assignment. The more advanced ones support networks in which a connection needs input, output and general signal processing configured at a node along a Label Switched Path (LSP). The work builds on earlier control of lambda and G.709-based networks. Two related documents are RFC 7446, a high-level information model, and RFC 7581, which supplies common encodings.
sections.eli5: Light beams of different colors carry data through glass cables. This RFC teaches the network's control messages how to say what should happen to each color along the way.

sections.title: Requirements for WSON Signaling
sections.content:
The requirements add to what GMPLS signaling already does. Signaling must carry enough about the signal for nodes, links and end systems to check compatibility and configure themselves. The details of local configuration are out of scope. The signal characteristics taken from RFC 6163 are the optical tributary signal class (modulation format), FEC, center frequency, bit rate and G-PID.

Nodes may also need to be told to process the signal, for example by 3R regeneration. RFC 6163 discussed three types: regeneration, fault and performance monitoring, and attribute conversion. Bidirectional LSPs must support both the same wavelength and different wavelengths in the two directions. Signaling should also let a particular distributed wavelength assignment method be selected, which helps fast recovery after an equipment failure.

Signaling of optical impairments is explicitly not addressed.
sections.eli5: Before handing a message to the next box, the sender must say what kind of light it is, whether to boost it, and which lanes both directions may use. Worries about the glass itself are left for someone else.

sections.title: Signaling Parameters and the Processing Hop Attribute TLV
sections.content:
LSPs signaled with these extensions MUST use Switching Capability WSON-LSC, Encoding Type Lambda and the label format from RFC 6205. The G-PID and bit rate already travel in the Generalized Label Request object and the RSVP SENDER_TSPEC and FLOWSPEC objects, so nothing new is needed for them.

To target one node, the RFC defines the WSON Processing Hop Attribute TLV, encoded as an attributes TLV (RFC 5420). It is carried in the ERO and RRO Hop Attributes subobjects and processed under RFC 7570. Its type value is 4.

The TLV holds sub-TLVs, each with a Type, a Length and a Value, padded with zeros to four-octet alignment. Sub-TLV order is significant and MUST be preserved.
sections.eli5: The note for one box is an envelope with labeled slips inside. The slips must stay in order, and each is padded to a standard size.

sections.title: The ResourceBlockInfo Sub-TLV
sections.content:
The ResourceBlockInfo sub-TLV (type 1, variable length) is a list of available Optical Interface Classes and processing capabilities, in the format of RFC 7581. At least one MUST be present, and no more than two SHOULD be. They MUST be processed in the order received, and extras SHOULD be ignored. Only the first RB Identifier in the RB Set is processed.

For a unidirectional LSP only one is processed and the I and O bits can be ignored. For a bidirectional LSP there MUST be either one sub-TLV with both I and O set to 1, or two sub-TLVs, one with only I set and one with only O set. A transit or egress node that finds a violation treats it as an error under RFC 7570.

A node adds the sub-TLV to an ERO Hop Attributes subobject for downstream nodes. Once a node parses it, the node allocates the indicated resources, such as a regeneration pool, and SHOULD report this in an RRO Hop Attributes subobject.
sections.eli5: This slip says which special equipment to use at a stop, such as a signal booster. The stop writes back what it actually used.

sections.title: The WavelengthSelection Sub-TLV
sections.content:
With Routing plus Distributed Wavelength Assignment (R+DWA), routing produces a path and the wavelength is chosen hop by hop. The WavelengthSelection sub-TLV (type 2, 8 octets with 2 octets of padding) states the direction rule and the method.

Its value has a W bit (1 bit) and a WA Method field (7 bits), followed by reserved bits. W = 0 requires the same wavelength in both directions, and 1 allows different wavelengths. A node that does not support a value MUST send a PathErr with Error Code 24 (Routing Problem) and sub-code 107 for the W bit or 108 for the method.

As with the other sub-TLV, a node SHOULD report the method it used in an RRO Hop Attributes subobject.
sections.eli5: This slip says which lane to pick and whether going and coming back must use the same lane. If a stop does not know the rule, it sends an error back.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document is built on the mechanisms of RFC 3473 and differs only in the information communicated. The additional information, optical resource and wavelength selection properties, is not viewed as substantively changing the security considerations of existing GMPLS signaling. The RFC points to RFC 3473 for the supported security measures and to RFC 5920 for an overview of GMPLS control plane vulnerabilities and protections.
sections.eli5: The notes are the same kind of notes the network already sends, so the old safety rules still cover them.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
IANA assigned type 4, WSON Processing Hop Attribute TLV, in the Attributes TLV Space registry. It is allowed on the RO LSP Attribute Subobject only. IANA also created two registries: one for sub-TLV types of this TLV (0 Reserved, 1 ResourceBlockInfo, 2 WavelengthSelection) and one for the Wavelength Assignment Method field. Assignments in both use Standards Action or Specification Required.

Two new sub-codes were added under Error Code 24, Routing Problem: 107 and 108.
sections.eli5: The numbers on the slips and the error codes were written into an official list so everyone uses them the same way.

items.label: Unspecified (any)
items.desc: Does not constrain the method; implied when the sub-TLV is absent.

items.label: First-Fit
items.desc: Chooses the available wavelength with the lowest index.

items.label: Least-Loaded (multi-fiber)
items.desc: Selects the wavelength with the largest residual capacity on the most loaded link along the route.
